arxiv-1910-11124.title: Enforcing Reasoning in Visual Commonsense Reasoning
arxiv-1910-11124.creator: Hammad A. Ayyubi Md. Mehrab Tanjim David J. Kriegman
arxiv-1910-11124.description: Abstract The task of Visual Commonsense Reasoning is extremely challenging in the sense that the model has to not only be able to answer a question given an image, but also be able to learn to reason. The baselines introduced in this task are quite limiting because two networks are trained for predicting answers and rationales separately.

arxiv-2105-02448.title: Nanoptera in nonlinear woodpile chains with zero precompression
arxiv-2105-02448.creator: G. Deng, C. J. Lustri
arxiv-2105-02448.description: Abstract We use exponential asymptotics to study travelling waves in woodpile systems modelled as singularly perturbed granular chains with zero precompression and small mass ratio. These systems are strongly nonlinear, and there is no analytic expression for their leading-order solution. We instead obtain an approximated leading-order solution using a hybrid numerical-analytic method.

arxiv-2105-14627.title: Space-Time Metasurfaces for Perfect Power Combining of Waves
arxiv-2105-14627.creator: X. Wang 1, V. S. Asadchy 2, S. Fan 2, S. A. Tretyakov 1
arxiv-2105-14627.description: Abstract In passive linear systems, complete combining of powers carried by waves from several input channels into a single output channel is forbidden by the energy conservation law. Here, we demonstrate that complete combination of both coherent and incoherent plane waves can be achieved using metasurfaces with properties varying in space and time.

arxiv-2111-06502.title: Enforcing essential boundary conditions on domains defined by point clouds
arxiv-2111-06502.creator: Frank Hartmann, Stefan Kollmannsberger
arxiv-2111-06502.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Frank Hartmann, Stefan Kollmannsberger. Abstract

This paper develops and investigates a new method for the application of Dirichlet boundary conditions for computational models defined by point clouds. Point cloud models often stem from laser or structured-light scanners which are used to scan existing mechanical structures for which CAD models either do not exist or from which the artifact under investigation deviates in shape or topology.

arxiv-2203-00289.title: Structured Output Feedback Control for Linear Quadratic Regulator Using Policy Gradient Method
arxiv-2203-00289.creator: Shokichi Takakura, Kazuhiro Sato
arxiv-2203-00289.description: Abstract We consider the static output feedback control for Linear Quadratic Regulator problems with structured constraints under the assumption that system parameters are unknown. To solve the problem in the model free setting, we propose the policy gradient algorithm based on the gradient projection method and show its global convergence to ε \varepsilon -stationary points.

arxiv-2301-07809.title: A Random Graph Growth Model
arxiv-2301-07809.creator: Michael Farber, Alexander Gnedin and Wajid Mannan
arxiv-2301-07809.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Michael Farber, Alexander Gnedin and Wajid Mannan. A growing random graph is constructed by successively sampling without replacement an element from the pool of virtual vertices and edges. At start of the process the pool contains N N virtual vertices and no edges. Each time a vertex is sampled and occupied, the edges linking the vertex to previously occupied vertices are added to the pool of virtual elements.

arxiv-2303-16445.title: Larger Probes Tell a Different Story: Extending Psycholinguistic Datasets Via In-Context Learning
arxiv-2303-16445.creator: Namrata Shivagunde, Vladislav Lialin, Anna Rumshisky
arxiv-2303-16445.description: Abstract Language model probing is often used to test specific capabilities of models. However, conclusions from such studies may be limited when the probing benchmarks are small and lack statistical power. In this work, we introduce new, larger datasets for negation (NEG-1500-SIMP) and role reversal (ROLE-1500) inspired by psycholinguistic studies.

arxiv-2305-13996.title: One-Shot Strategically Deconflicted Route and Operational Volume Generation for Urban Air Mobility Operations
arxiv-2305-13996.creator: Ellis L. Thompson, Yan Xu, Peng Wei
arxiv-2305-13996.description: Abstract In the UAM space, strategic deconfliction provides an all-essential layer to airspace automation by providing safe, pre-emptive deconfliction or assignment of airspace resources to airspace users pre-flight. Strategic deconfliction approaches provide an elegant solution to pre-flight deconfliction operations. This overall creates safer and more efficient airspace and reduces the workload on controllers.

arxiv-2306-04357.title: Dial-MAE: ConTextual Masked Auto-Encoder for Retrieval-based Dialogue Systems
arxiv-2306-04357.creator: Zhenpeng Su, Xing Wu, Wei Zhou, Guangyuan Ma, Songlin Hu
arxiv-2306-04357.description: Abstract Dialogue response selection aims to select an appropriate response from several candidates based on a given user and system utterance history. Most existing works primarily focus on post-training and fine-tuning tailored for cross-encoders. However, there are no post-training methods tailored for dense encoders in dialogue response selection.

arxiv-2308-03228.title: Why Linguistics Will Thrive in the 21st Century: A Reply to Piantadosi (2023)
arxiv-2308-03228.creator: Jordan Kodner, Sarah Payne, Jeffrey Heinz
arxiv-2308-03228.description: Abstract \noautomath 1 Introduction We present a critical assessment of Piantadosi, 2023 ’s ( Piantadosi, 2023 ) claim that “Modern language models refute Chomsky’s approach to language,” focusing on four main points. First, despite the impressive performance and utility of large language models (LLMs), humans achieve their capacity for language after exposure to several orders of magnitude less data.

arxiv-2404-14296.title: Does Your Neural Code Completion Model Use My Code? A Membership Inference Approach CCS: Security and privacy Software security engineering
arxiv-2404-14296.creator: Yao Wan, Guanghua Wan, Shijie Zhang, Hongyu Zhang, Yulei Sui, Pan Zhou, Hai Jin, Lichao sun
arxiv-2404-14296.description: Abstract . Recent years have witnessed significant progress in developing deep learning-based models for automated code completion. Examples of such models include CodeGPT and StarCoder. These models are typically trained from a large amount of source code collected from open-source communities such as GitHub.

arxiv-2410-22971.title: Private Synthetic Text Generation with Diffusion Models
arxiv-2410-22971.creator: Sebastian Ochs, Ivan HabernalTrustworthy Human Language Technologies
arxiv-2410-22971.description: Abstract How capable are diffusion models of generating synthetics texts? Recent research shows their strengths, with performance reaching that of auto-regressive LLMs. But are they also good in generating synthetic data if the training was under differential privacy? Here the evidence is missing, yet the promises from private image generation look strong.

arxiv-2412-06614.title: MVReward: Better Aligning and Evaluating Multi-View Diffusion Models with Human Preferences
arxiv-2412-06614.creator: Weitao Wang, Haoran Xu, Yuxiao Yang, Zhifang Liu, Jun Meng, Haoqian Wang
arxiv-2412-06614.description: Abstract Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in 3D content generation. However, corresponding evaluation methods struggle to keep pace. Automatic approaches have proven challenging to align with human preferences, and the mixed comparison of text- and image-driven methods often leads to unfair evaluations.

arxiv-2503-08444.title: Computation Kernel for Feynman Diagrams
arxiv-2503-08444.creator: Daria Gazizova, Rayan Farid, B. D. E. McNiven, I. Assi, Ethan G. Armstrong, J. P. F. LeBlanc
arxiv-2503-08444.description: Abstract We present a general representation for solving problems in many-body perturbation theory. By defining an overcomplete representation for the single-particle Green’s function we show how one can convert an arbitrary Feynman graph to a universal kernel representation. Once constructed, the computation kernel contains no problem specific information yet contains all explicit temperature and frequency dependence of the diagram.

arxiv-2503-14269.title: DARS: Dynamic Action Re-Sampling to Enhance Coding Agent Performance by Adaptive Tree Traversal
arxiv-2503-14269.creator: Vaibhav AggarwalSprinklr, Ojasv Kamal Mirelo AI, Abhinav JapeshSprinklr, Zhijing JinMPI-IS & University of Toronto, Bernhard SchölkopfMPI for Intelligent Systems
arxiv-2503-14269.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized various domains, including natural language processing, data analysis, and software development, by enabling automation. In software engineering, LLM-powered coding agents have garnered significant attention due to their potential to automate complex development tasks, assist in debugging, and enhance productivity.

arxiv-2509-04446.title: Plot’n Polish : Zero-shot Story Visualization and Disentangled Editing with Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
arxiv-2509-04446.creator: Kiymet Akdemir, Jing Shi, Kushal Kafle, Brian Price, Pinar Yanardag
arxiv-2509-04446.description: Abstract Text-to-image diffusion models have demonstrated significant capabilities to generate diverse and detailed visuals in various domains, and story visualization is emerging as a particularly promising application. However, as their use in real-world creative domains increases, the need for providing enhanced control, refinement, and the ability to modify images post-generation in a consistent manner becomes an important challenge.

arxiv-2509-15004.title: Fourier heuristic PINNs to solve the biharmonic equations based on its coupled scheme Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2509-15004.creator: Yujia Huang, Xi’an Li, Jinran Wu
arxiv-2509-15004.description: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have been widely utilized for solving a range of partial differential equations (PDEs) in various scientific and engineering disciplines. This paper presents a Fourier heuristic-enhanced PINN (termed FCPINN) designed to address a specific class of biharmonic equations with Dirichlet and Navier boundary conditions.

arxiv-2511-01583.title: Federated Cyber Defense: Privacy-Preserving Ransomware Detection Across Distributed Systems
arxiv-2511-01583.creator: Sherpa.ai research@sherpa.ai
arxiv-2511-01583.description: Abstract Detecting malware, especially ransomware, is essential to securing today’s interconnected ecosystems, including cloud storage, enterprise file-sharing, and database services. Training high-performing artificial intelligence (AI) detectors requires diverse datasets, which are often distributed across multiple organizations, making centralization necessary. However, centralized learning is often impractical due to security, privacy regulations, data ownership issues, and legal barriers to cross-organizational sharing.

arxiv-2601-11146.title: Inverse spectral problem with low regularity refractive index
arxiv-2601-11146.creator: Kewen Bu, Youjun Deng, Yan Jiang, Kai Zhang
arxiv-2601-11146.description: Abstract . This article investigates the unique determination of a radial refractive index n n from spectral data. First, we demonstrate that for piecewise twice continuously differentiable functions, n n is not uniquely determined by the special transmission eigenvalues associated with radially symmetric eigenfunctions.

pmc-10649832.title: Radiation Protection of a 3D Computer Tomography Scanning Workplace for Logs—A Case Study
pmc-10649832.creator: Tomáš Gergeľ, Juraj Hamza, Vojtěch Ondrejka, Miroslav Němec, Miroslav Vanek, Jennifer Drugdová
pmc-10649832.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Despite its undeniable advantages, the operation of a CT scanner also carries risks to human health. The CT scanner is a source of ionizing radiation, which also affects people in its surroundings. The aim of this paper is to quantify the radiation exposure of workers at a 3D CT wood scanning workplace and to determine a monitoring program based on measurements of ionizing radiation levels during the operation of a CT log scanner.

pmc-10656920.title: The relationship between family function and the incidence of overweight/obesity in children and adolescents in Chengdu city, Sichuan province of China: based on latent profile analysis
pmc-10656920.creator: Xixi Jiang, Xiufang Zhao, Junxia Zhou, Xiujuan Zhang, Yan Song, Li Zhao
pmc-10656920.description: BackgroundOverweight/obesity in children and adolescents has become a global health problem, and family function may be associated with its occurrence. Studies exploring the association between family function and overweight/obesity in children and adolescents were performed in Western and Taiwan, China. To date, related studies haven’t been conducted in Mainland China.

pmc-11324956.title: Dynamic cell culture modulates colon cancer cell migration in a novel 3D cell culture system
pmc-11324956.creator: M. Mohamadian Namaqi, F. Moll, S. Wiedemeier, A. Grodrian, K. Lemke
pmc-11324956.description: The progression of cancer cell migration, invasion and subsequent metastasis is the main cause of mortality in cancer patients. Through creating more accurate cancer models, we can achieve more precise results, which will lead to a better understanding of the invasion process. This holds promise for more effective prevention and treatment strategies.

pmc-11625075.title: Changing the Inoculum Type From Preculture to Spore Suspension Markedly Alters the Production of Secondary Metabolites in Filamentous Microbial Coculture
pmc-11625075.creator: Tomasz Boruta, Weronika Pawlikowska, Martyna Foryś, Grzegorz Englart, Anna Ścigaczewska
pmc-11625075.description: The shake flask cocultures of Aspergillus terreus and Streptomyces rimosus were investigated with regard to the production of mevinolinic acid (lovastatin), oxytetracycline, and other secondary metabolites (SMs). The aim of the study was to determine the effect of inoculum type (spore suspension or preculture) on the levels of SMs in the fermentation broth.

pmc-11964815.title: m6A RNA甲基化在肾脏固有细胞损伤中的作用
pmc-11964815.creator: 自霞 赵, 晨 张, 私 吴, 军军 栾, 华 周
pmc-11964815.description: RNA甲基化修饰是一种高度动态且可逆的表观遗传学调控机制，主要受甲基转移酶、去甲基化酶、甲基化阅读蛋白3种因子调控。N6-甲基腺嘌呤(N6-methyladenosine，m6A)甲基化修饰是最常见的一种RNA甲基化修饰形式，当该过程出现异常的时候，可能引起多种疾病的发生。肾脏疾病因其发病率高、预后差、造成的社会经济负担重而备受关注。肾脏固有细胞损伤参与多种肾脏疾病的发生、发展过程中。深入探究肾脏固有细胞的损伤机制对肾脏疾病的防治具有深远意义。近年来，研究发现m6A RNA甲基化在肾脏固有细胞损伤过程中发挥重要作用，其有望成为肾脏疾病治疗的新靶点。 肾脏疾病是一个重要的公共卫生问题[1]。慢性肾脏病(chronic kidney disease，CKD)作为一种常见的肾脏疾病，发病率高，并且会加重心血管疾病以及其他疾病的负担，大幅增加病死率，对个人健康和社会经济造成巨大负担。CKD患病率高，最新一项横断面研究[2]发现，2018至2019年，中国有8 200万成年人患有CKD。此外，全球每年有超过1 300万人受到急性肾损伤(acute kidney injury，AKI)的影响，并有170万人因此死亡[3]。肾脏疾病涵盖由多种原因引发的肾脏固有细胞损伤，这些细胞包括足细胞、肾小球系膜细胞、肾小球内皮细胞、肾小管上皮细胞等，其分布于肾脏不同的位置，并具有独特的功能。在各种肾脏疾病的发生和发展过程中，不同的肾脏固有细胞发生损伤，如足细胞损伤是局灶节段性肾小球硬化症(focal segmental glomerular sclerosis，FSGS)中肾小球的典型病理改变[4]，肾小管上皮细胞损伤是AKI的标志之一[5]。 甲基化是从活性甲基化合物上将甲基催化转移到其他化合物的过程。在生物体中，甲基化作为一种结构修饰方式，可通过引发表观遗传学改变来调节基因表达，而不影响基因序列。甲基化可以发生在各种生物分子中，包括DNA、RNA及蛋白质。RNA作为重要的基因表达中间产物，在转录和翻译过程中受结构修饰的调节，这一过程统称为表观转录组学。近年来研究发现，RNA甲基化参与调控多种疾病，包括癌症[6]、心血管疾病[7]和神经系统疾病[8]等。N6-甲基腺苷(N6-methyladenosine，m6A)甲基化是信使RNA(messenger RNA，mRNA)中最丰富的内部甲基化修饰形式，并且已成为广泛调控各种生理过程中基因表达的机制[9]。 m6A甲基化作为最常见的mRNA修饰，在肾脏固有细胞损伤过程中有重要意义[10]。研究[11]发现在阿霉素诱导的FSGS模型小鼠中，足细胞内m6A RNA水平升高，甲基转移酶样蛋白(methyltransferase-like protein，METTL)14表达显著上调；在敲除足细胞中的METTL14后，足细胞损伤减轻。深入探究m6A RNA甲基化在肾脏细胞损伤中的作用，有望为肾脏疾病的治疗提供新的思路和视角。 m6A RNA甲基化修饰相关酶和蛋白质 RNA甲基化修饰是高度动态和可逆的，受甲基转移酶(writer)、去甲基化酶(eraser)、甲基化阅读蛋白(reader)3种因子调控，甲基转移酶通常形成多蛋白复合物来催化RNA甲基化，而去甲基化酶则会将RNA去甲基化，修饰过的甲基化位点则被甲基化阅读蛋白识别(图1)。RNA甲基化修饰影响RNA剪接和mRNA的定位、翻译、转位和稳定性，从而调控基因的表达[12]。m6A是指在腺嘌呤的第6位氮原子上加1个甲基，它是最早被发现的甲基化修饰，也是高等真核生物中最常见的RNA甲基化修饰方式。 m6A RNA甲基化修饰 Figure 1 m6A RNA methylation modification m6A: N6-methyladenosine; mRNA: messenger RNA; RBM15: RNA binding motif protein 15; ZC3H13: Zinc finger CCCH domain-containing protein 13; WTAP: Wilms’ tumor 1-associating protein; METTL3: Methyltransferase-like protein 3; METTL14: Methyltransferase-like protein 14;

pmc-12522861.title: Process evaluation of the adolescent and youth health program implementation in primary healthcare facilities of Woliso town, Oromia regional state, Ethiopia: a case study evaluation design
pmc-12522861.creator: Kebede Wegi Feyisa, Negalign Berhanu Bayou, Yibeltal Siraneh, Bekele Wegi Feyisa
pmc-12522861.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn Ethiopia, adolescents and youth continue to experience a high burden of morbidity and mortality related to reproductive health problems. However, the implementation of the adolescents and youth health program in Woliso Town has not yet been evaluated. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the process of the program implementation in the primary healthcare facilities of Woliso Town, Oromia Regional State, Ethiopia.MethodsA convergent parallel case study design with a formative evaluation approach was employed from May 21 to June 20, 2023.

pmc-12615354.title: Network analysis of antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus: characterization of hub genes and their functional implications
pmc-12615354.creator: Md Imran Hasan, Davida S Smyth, Ashley I Teufel
pmc-12615354.description: Staphylococcus aureus is a pathogenic bacterium that is increasingly resistant to antibiotics. To identify genes that facilitate this resistance, we analyzed 1062 genomes from the NCBI Genome database. From these genomes, we compile a list of 229 antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes from the CARD, ResFinder, MEGARes, and AR-ANNOT databases.

pmc-13061219.title: Association of marital and parental status with stress, support, adherence, and quality of life among breast cancer women
pmc-13061219.creator: Laraib Akram, Ghulam Abbas, Haris Khurram, Ayesha Aslam, Fawad Ahmad Randhawa, Abdullah A. Assiri, Shahid Shah, Mukhtiar Baig, Mukhtiar Baig, Mukhtiar Baig, Mukhtiar Baig
pmc-13061219.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundsBreast cancer presents multifaceted challenges that extend beyond physical illness, profoundly influencing patients’ psychological well-being, treatment adherence, and social relationships. Marital and parental status further affect these experiences by influencing coping capacity, emotional stability, and perceived support systems.

pmc-13070891.title: Multifaceted Interventions Based on Education and Recognition to Enhance Nurses' Compliance With Standard Precautions: A Quasi‐Experimental Design
pmc-13070891.creator: Menevse Yildirim, Seyda Seren Intepeler, Simon Ching Lam
pmc-13070891.description: This study examines the effect of multifaceted interventions based on education (1) and recognition (2) of compliance with standard precautions (SPs). A quasi‐experimental research design with a one‐group pre‐test and post‐test was used. The purposive sample included 71 nurses working in different specialty units at a large hospital in Turkey.

pmc-13582057.title: Antimicrobial-resistant organism carriage and metagenomic characterization of the microbiome and resistome in veterinary workers
pmc-13582057.creator: Laurel E. Redding, Weiming Hu, Scott Daniel, Maho Okumura, Maeve E. Hiehle, Michael Z. David, Lynn Hunter, Stephen D. Cole

However, the extent to which these occupational exposures influence their carriage of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) organisms and the composition of their microbiome and resistome remains poorly understood.

pmc-13628706.title: Site‐specific O‐glycans influence lacritin structure and multimerization in tears
pmc-13628706.creator: Vincent Chang, Ryan J Chen, Isaac Lian, Madilynn Hamilton, Keira E Mahoney, Jeff Romano, Gordon Laurie, Stacy A Malaker
pmc-13628706.description: Lacritin is an abundantly expressed glycoprotein in tear fluid and plays key roles in immune response, tear secretion, and bacterial killing. These biological functions are tightly regulated through several biochemical mechanisms including multimerization, proteolysis, and alternative splicing, especially within its C‐terminal domain.

pmc-13671087.title: Monomeric C-reactive protein potentiates microglia-mediated neuroinflammation in Alzheimer’s disease via the PLC-PKC-MAPK-NF-κB pathway
pmc-13671087.creator: Jie Zhang, Yiyi Zhu, Qishan Zhang, Yuting Dai, Hang Liu, Jingming Shi, Yanghua Jiang, Qian Chen
pmc-13671087.description: Neuroinflammation is a major contributor to the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Although elevated serum C-reactive protein (CRP) is associated with increased AD risk, the specific conformational forms of CRP operative in the brain and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
